answer: Memory-hard per-identity proofs resist sybils: each identity must compute a memory-hard function with a large RAM working set, poorly parallelizable, to act, so concurrent identities cannot share one allocation — running a garden of fakes demands N times the memory, not N times a cheap hash. A grove of co-located accounts on one box contends for the same RAM and serializes, while the karst-porous access pattern defeats precompute and ASIC shortcuts. Cost scales with simultaneous identities held, so a swarm pays linearly in hardware it cannot fake away.
